misconceptions.label: Abnormal uterine bleeding
misconceptions.misconception: Heavy menstrual bleeding in a woman over 45 can be treated as hormonal without evaluation.
misconceptions.correction: Endometrial sampling is needed to exclude hyperplasia or cancer in older women or those with risk factors.

misconceptions.label: Acid-base disorders
misconceptions.misconception: A normal pH excludes an acid-base disorder.
misconceptions.correction: Mixed disorders or full compensation can give a normal pH; check bicarbonate, PaCO2 and anion gap.

misconceptions.label: Acute coronary syndrome
misconceptions.misconception: A normal first ECG rules out acute coronary syndrome.
misconceptions.correction: Up to half of early ECGs are non-diagnostic; repeat ECGs and serial troponins are needed before ruling it out.

misconceptions.label: Acute gastroenteritis
misconceptions.misconception: Children with diarrhoea should stop feeding to rest the gut.
misconceptions.correction: Continue breastfeeding and feeding; give ORS and zinc.

misconceptions.label: Acute kidney injury
misconceptions.misconception: Serum creatinine rises immediately after kidney injury.
misconceptions.correction: Creatinine lags behind injury by 24–48 hours; urine output and trends matter early.

misconceptions.label: Acute scrotum
misconceptions.misconception: Testicular torsion should be confirmed with ultrasound before surgery.
misconceptions.correction: Suspected torsion needs urgent surgical exploration; imaging must not delay it.

misconceptions.label: Acute suppurative otitis media
misconceptions.misconception: Every case of acute otitis media needs antibiotics immediately.
misconceptions.correction: Many cases resolve spontaneously; watchful waiting is reasonable in selected older children without severe features.

misconceptions.label: Adrenal insufficiency
misconceptions.misconception: Steroids can be stopped suddenly after long-term use.
misconceptions.correction: Long-term steroids suppress the axis; abrupt withdrawal can cause adrenal crisis, so taper.

misconceptions.label: Advanced life support
misconceptions.misconception: Asystole should be treated with defibrillation.
misconceptions.correction: Asystole and PEA are non-shockable; give CPR and adrenaline and treat reversible causes.

misconceptions.label: Adverse drug reactions
misconceptions.misconception: An adverse drug reaction means the drug was given incorrectly.
misconceptions.correction: ADRs can occur with correct use at normal doses; they should still be reported to pharmacovigilance.

misconceptions.label: Adverse events following immunisation
misconceptions.misconception: Any illness after vaccination was caused by the vaccine.
misconceptions.correction: Temporal association is not causation; AEFIs are investigated and classified before attributing cause.

misconceptions.label: Airway management
misconceptions.misconception: Pulse oximetry confirms correct endotracheal tube placement.
misconceptions.correction: Capnography (end-tidal CO2) confirms tracheal placement; saturation falls late.

misconceptions.label: Amblyopia
misconceptions.misconception: A lazy eye can be treated at any age with equal success.
misconceptions.correction: Amblyopia responds best in early childhood within the visual development period.

misconceptions.label: Amyloidosis
misconceptions.misconception: Amyloid is a single protein that causes one disease.
misconceptions.correction: Amyloid is a misfolded beta-pleated structure formed by different proteins (AL, AA, ATTR), each with different causes.

misconceptions.label: Anaemia
misconceptions.misconception: All anaemia in women is iron deficiency and can be treated with iron without tests.
misconceptions.correction: Red cell indices and iron studies are needed; thalassaemia trait and B12 or folate deficiency need different management.

misconceptions.label: Anaemia in pregnancy
misconceptions.misconception: Haemoglobin falls in pregnancy only because of iron deficiency.
misconceptions.correction: Physiological haemodilution lowers haemoglobin; iron deficiency is common but pregnancy has its own cut-offs.

misconceptions.label: Angle-closure glaucoma
misconceptions.misconception: Dilating drops are safe in a patient with an acute painful red eye and halos.
misconceptions.correction: Mydriatics can precipitate or worsen angle closure; this presentation needs urgent pressure lowering.

misconceptions.label: Antepartum haemorrhage
misconceptions.misconception: A vaginal examination is the first step in painless bleeding late in pregnancy.
misconceptions.correction: Placenta praevia must be excluded by ultrasound before any digital vaginal examination.

misconceptions.label: Antibacterial drugs
misconceptions.misconception: Antibiotics help viral upper respiratory infections by preventing secondary infection.
misconceptions.correction: Routine antibiotics do not prevent complications in viral URTI and drive resistance and side effects.

misconceptions.label: Anticoagulants
misconceptions.misconception: Heparin and warfarin are monitored with the same test.
misconceptions.correction: Unfractionated heparin is monitored with aPTT; warfarin with PT/INR.

misconceptions.label: Antidepressants
misconceptions.misconception: Antidepressants work fully within the first few days.
misconceptions.correction: Mood benefit usually takes 2–6 weeks; side effects appear earlier.

misconceptions.label: Antidiabetic drugs
misconceptions.misconception: Metformin commonly causes hypoglycaemia.
misconceptions.correction: Metformin alone rarely causes hypoglycaemia; sulfonylureas and insulin do.

misconceptions.label: Antihypertensive drugs
misconceptions.misconception: Beta-blockers are first-line for all hypertension.
misconceptions.correction: First-line choice depends on age, ethnicity and comorbidity; beta-blockers are not first-line for uncomplicated hypertension.

misconceptions.label: Antimicrobial resistance
misconceptions.misconception: Resistance develops because the patient's body becomes used to the antibiotic.
misconceptions.correction: Bacteria, not patients, become resistant through selection and gene transfer driven by antibiotic exposure.

misconceptions.label: Antimicrobial stewardship
misconceptions.misconception: Broader-spectrum antibiotics are always safer.
misconceptions.correction: Use the narrowest effective agent; de-escalate once culture results are known.

misconceptions.label: Antiplatelet drugs
misconceptions.misconception: Aspirin works by dissolving existing clots.
misconceptions.correction: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits platelet COX-1 to prevent new clot formation; fibrinolytics dissolve clots.

misconceptions.label: Antipsychotics
misconceptions.misconception: Atypical antipsychotics have no important side effects.
misconceptions.correction: They cause weight gain, diabetes and dyslipidaemia; metabolic monitoring is needed.

misconceptions.label: Antiseizure medicines
misconceptions.misconception: Valproate is the preferred antiseizure medicine in women of childbearing age.
misconceptions.correction: Valproate is highly teratogenic; avoid it in women who may become pregnant unless no alternative exists.

misconceptions.label: Antitubercular drugs
misconceptions.misconception: Isoniazid-related neuropathy is prevented by vitamin B12.
misconceptions.correction: Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) prevents isoniazid peripheral neuropathy.

misconceptions.label: Anxiety disorders
misconceptions.misconception: Benzodiazepines are the best long-term treatment for anxiety disorders.
misconceptions.correction: SSRIs and psychological therapy are first-line; benzodiazepines cause dependence and are for short-term use.

misconceptions.label: Appendicitis
misconceptions.misconception: Appendicitis always starts with pain in the right iliac fossa.
misconceptions.correction: Pain classically starts periumbilical and migrates; retrocaecal and pelvic positions and pregnancy change the picture.

misconceptions.label: Association and causation
misconceptions.misconception: A statistically significant association proves causation.
misconceptions.correction: Causation needs consideration of bias, confounding, temporality and criteria such as Bradford Hill.

misconceptions.label: Asthma
misconceptions.misconception: Wheeze is always present in a severe asthma attack.
misconceptions.correction: A silent chest signals life-threatening asthma with minimal air movement.

misconceptions.label: Basic life support
misconceptions.misconception: Check the pulse for a full minute before starting CPR.
misconceptions.correction: Pulse checks should take no more than 10 seconds; start compressions if unresponsive without normal breathing.

misconceptions.label: Bipolar disorder
misconceptions.misconception: Antidepressants alone are good treatment for bipolar depression.
misconceptions.correction: Antidepressant monotherapy can trigger mania; mood stabilisers are central.

misconceptions.label: Blood culture
misconceptions.misconception: Blood cultures can be taken after starting antibiotics without loss of yield.
misconceptions.correction: Antibiotics reduce culture yield; take cultures before the first dose whenever possible.

misconceptions.label: Blood gas analysis
misconceptions.misconception: Compensation fully corrects pH in chronic acid-base disorders.
misconceptions.correction: Compensation is usually incomplete; overcorrection suggests a second primary disorder.

misconceptions.label: Blood groups
misconceptions.misconception: A person with blood group O can receive blood from any group.
misconceptions.correction: Group O individuals have anti-A and anti-B antibodies; group O is the universal red cell donor, AB the universal recipient.

misconceptions.label: Blood pressure
misconceptions.misconception: Mean arterial pressure is the average of systolic and diastolic pressure.
misconceptions.correction: Because diastole lasts longer, MAP is approximately diastolic plus one-third of pulse pressure.

misconceptions.label: Breast cancer
misconceptions.misconception: A painless breast lump is less worrying than a painful one.
misconceptions.correction: Most breast cancers are painless; any new lump needs triple assessment.

misconceptions.label: Breastfeeding
misconceptions.misconception: Babies need water in addition to breast milk in hot weather in the first six months.
misconceptions.correction: Exclusive breastfeeding meets all water needs in the first six months.

misconceptions.label: Bronchiectasis
misconceptions.misconception: Bronchiectasis is diagnosed reliably on chest X-ray.
misconceptions.correction: High-resolution CT is the diagnostic test; plain films are often normal or non-specific.

misconceptions.label: Burns
misconceptions.misconception: Ice and butter should be applied to burns.
misconceptions.correction: Cool with running tap water for about 20 minutes; ice and home remedies worsen injury.

misconceptions.label: Cardiac biomarkers
misconceptions.misconception: Troponin rises within minutes of myocardial injury, so a single early value is enough.
misconceptions.correction: Troponin takes about 3–6 hours to rise with conventional assays; serial testing is needed, and it also rises in non-ischaemic injury.

misconceptions.label: Cardiac cycle
misconceptions.misconception: The first heart sound is caused by closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves.
misconceptions.correction: S1 is mitral and tricuspid closure at the start of systole; S2 is aortic and pulmonary closure.

misconceptions.label: Cardiac output
misconceptions.misconception: Increasing heart rate always increases cardiac output.
misconceptions.correction: At very high rates diastolic filling time falls, so stroke volume and cardiac output can drop.

misconceptions.label: Cataract
misconceptions.misconception: A cataract must be 'ripe' before surgery.
misconceptions.correction: Surgery is done when vision affects daily life; waiting for maturity is outdated.

misconceptions.label: Cerumen impaction
misconceptions.misconception: Earwax should be cleaned regularly with cotton buds.
misconceptions.correction: Wax is protective and self-clearing; cotton buds push it deeper and can injure the canal.

misconceptions.label: Cervical cancer
misconceptions.misconception: Cervical cancer screening is only needed after symptoms appear.
misconceptions.correction: Screening detects pre-invasive disease in asymptomatic women; HPV infection is the necessary cause.

misconceptions.label: Chest trauma
misconceptions.misconception: Tension pneumothorax should be confirmed by chest X-ray before treatment.
misconceptions.correction: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis needing immediate decompression.

misconceptions.label: Cholesteatoma
misconceptions.misconception: Cholesteatoma is a benign condition that can be managed with drops.
misconceptions.correction: Cholesteatoma is locally destructive and needs surgery to prevent intracranial and other complications.

misconceptions.label: Chronic kidney disease
misconceptions.misconception: Small kidneys are required to diagnose chronic kidney disease.
misconceptions.correction: Kidneys may be normal-sized or large in diabetic nephropathy, amyloidosis and polycystic disease.

misconceptions.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
misconceptions.misconception: Oxygen should be given to reach 100% saturation in COPD exacerbation.
misconceptions.correction: In patients at risk of hypercapnia, target saturations of about 88–92% to avoid worsening CO2 retention.

misconceptions.label: Cirrhosis
misconceptions.misconception: Cirrhosis is caused only by alcohol.
misconceptions.correction: Viral hepatitis B and C, fatty liver disease, autoimmune and metabolic diseases are major causes.

misconceptions.label: Cold chain
misconceptions.misconception: Freezing is safe for all vaccines.
misconceptions.correction: Freeze-sensitive vaccines (e.g. pentavalent, hepatitis B, TT) are damaged by freezing; the shake test detects this.

misconceptions.label: Colorectal carcinoma
misconceptions.misconception: Rectal bleeding in an older adult can be attributed to haemorrhoids without further tests.
misconceptions.correction: New rectal bleeding or a change in bowel habit in older adults needs evaluation for colorectal cancer.

misconceptions.label: Corticosteroids
misconceptions.misconception: Inhaled steroids give quick relief in an asthma attack.
misconceptions.correction: Inhaled steroids control inflammation over time; short-acting beta-agonists give quick relief.

misconceptions.label: COVID-19
misconceptions.misconception: Antibiotics treat COVID-19 pneumonia.
misconceptions.correction: COVID-19 is viral; antibiotics are for documented or strongly suspected bacterial co-infection only.

misconceptions.label: Cushing syndrome
misconceptions.misconception: The commonest cause of Cushing syndrome is a pituitary adenoma.
misconceptions.correction: Exogenous glucocorticoid use is the commonest cause; Cushing disease is the commonest endogenous cause.

misconceptions.label: Cyanosis
misconceptions.misconception: Cyanosis is a reliable sign of hypoxia in anaemic patients.
misconceptions.correction: Cyanosis needs about 5 g/dL of deoxygenated haemoglobin, so severe anaemia can mask hypoxia.

misconceptions.label: Delirium
misconceptions.misconception: Delirium in older adults is usually hyperactive and obvious.
misconceptions.correction: Hypoactive delirium is common and easily missed as depression or tiredness; screen actively.

misconceptions.label: Dementia
misconceptions.misconception: Memory loss in older people is a normal part of ageing.
misconceptions.correction: Progressive memory loss that affects daily function is not normal ageing and needs evaluation for dementia and reversible causes.

misconceptions.label: Depression
misconceptions.misconception: Asking about suicide may put the idea into a patient's mind.
misconceptions.correction: Asking directly about suicidal thoughts does not increase risk and is essential for assessment.

misconceptions.label: Dermatophytosis
misconceptions.misconception: Topical steroid-antifungal combinations are good treatment for ringworm.
misconceptions.correction: Steroid combinations worsen and disguise tinea and contribute to chronic, resistant infection.

misconceptions.label: Developmental milestones
misconceptions.misconception: Preterm infants should meet milestones at the same chronological age as term infants.
misconceptions.correction: Use corrected age for preterm infants until about two years.

misconceptions.label: Diabetes in pregnancy
misconceptions.misconception: Oral antidiabetic drugs are always contraindicated in pregnancy.
misconceptions.correction: Insulin is standard, but metformin is used in selected cases of gestational diabetes.

misconceptions.label: Diabetes mellitus
misconceptions.misconception: Glucose in the urine is a reliable test for diagnosing diabetes.
misconceptions.correction: Glycosuria depends on the renal threshold; diagnosis uses plasma glucose or HbA1c.

misconceptions.label: Diabetic emergencies
misconceptions.misconception: In diabetic ketoacidosis insulin should be started before checking potassium.
misconceptions.correction: Check potassium first; insulin drives potassium into cells and can cause dangerous hypokalaemia if it is already low.

misconceptions.label: Diabetic ketoacidosis
misconceptions.misconception: Children in DKA need rapid large fluid boluses.
misconceptions.correction: Fluids are given more cautiously in children because of the risk of cerebral oedema.

misconceptions.label: Diabetic retinopathy
misconceptions.misconception: Good vision means there is no diabetic retinopathy.
misconceptions.correction: Sight-threatening retinopathy can be present with normal acuity; regular fundus screening is needed.

misconceptions.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
misconceptions.misconception: DIC is only a bleeding disorder.
misconceptions.correction: DIC involves widespread microthrombi and consumption of factors and platelets; organ damage from thrombosis is common.

misconceptions.label: Diuretics
misconceptions.misconception: Loop and thiazide diuretics have the same effect on calcium.
misconceptions.correction: Loop diuretics increase calcium excretion; thiazides reduce it.

misconceptions.label: Drug interactions
misconceptions.misconception: Enzyme inducers increase the effect of drugs metabolised by that enzyme.
misconceptions.correction: Inducers speed metabolism and reduce effect (e.g. rifampicin with oral contraceptives); inhibitors increase it.

misconceptions.label: Drug-resistant tuberculosis
misconceptions.misconception: Adding a single new drug to a failing TB regimen is a reasonable step.
misconceptions.correction: Adding one drug to a failing regimen promotes further resistance; regimens are changed on the basis of drug-susceptibility testing.

misconceptions.label: Drugs for asthma and COPD
misconceptions.misconception: A short-acting reliever alone is adequate long-term treatment for persistent asthma.
misconceptions.correction: Persistent asthma needs inhaled corticosteroid-based controller therapy.

misconceptions.label: Drugs used in heart failure
misconceptions.misconception: Digoxin improves survival in heart failure.
misconceptions.correction: Digoxin reduces symptoms and admissions but not mortality; ACE inhibitors or ARNI, beta-blockers, MRAs and SGLT2 inhibitors improve survival.

misconceptions.label: Dying declaration
misconceptions.misconception: A dying declaration is invalid unless recorded by a magistrate.
misconceptions.correction: A magistrate is preferred, but a doctor or others can record it if needed; the declarant must be of sound mind.

misconceptions.label: Dysentery
misconceptions.misconception: All bloody diarrhoea is amoebic.
misconceptions.correction: Shigella is the commonest cause of bloody diarrhoea in children; stool examination guides treatment.

misconceptions.label: Dysplasia
misconceptions.misconception: Dysplasia is the same as cancer.
misconceptions.correction: Dysplasia is disordered growth that may regress; it becomes invasive cancer only after the basement membrane is breached.

misconceptions.label: Ectopic pregnancy
misconceptions.misconception: A normal-looking uterus on ultrasound with a positive pregnancy test excludes ectopic pregnancy.
misconceptions.correction: An empty uterus with a positive test is a pregnancy of unknown location and ectopic must be actively excluded with serial beta-hCG and scans.

misconceptions.label: Electrocardiogram
misconceptions.misconception: The T wave represents atrial repolarisation.
misconceptions.correction: The T wave is ventricular repolarisation; atrial repolarisation is hidden in the QRS complex.

misconceptions.label: Electroconvulsive therapy
misconceptions.misconception: ECT is outdated and causes permanent brain damage.
misconceptions.correction: ECT under anaesthesia is safe and highly effective for severe depression and catatonia; memory effects are usually temporary.

misconceptions.label: Embolism
misconceptions.misconception: Pulmonary embolism always causes chest pain and haemoptysis.
misconceptions.correction: Unexplained breathlessness and tachycardia are the commonest features; the classic triad is often absent.

misconceptions.label: Encephalitis
misconceptions.misconception: Encephalitis and meningitis present identically.
misconceptions.correction: Encephalitis causes altered behaviour, consciousness and seizures early; meningitis is dominated by meningeal signs.

misconceptions.label: Endocrine pancreas
misconceptions.misconception: Glucagon and insulin are secreted by the same cells.
misconceptions.correction: Insulin comes from beta cells and glucagon from alpha cells of the islets.

misconceptions.label: Enteric fever
misconceptions.misconception: The Widal test in the first week reliably confirms typhoid.
misconceptions.correction: Blood culture is the test of choice in the first week; Widal has poor sensitivity and specificity, especially in endemic areas.

misconceptions.label: Envenomation
misconceptions.misconception: A tourniquet and incision help a snakebite victim.
misconceptions.correction: Tourniquets, incision and suction are harmful; immobilise the limb and transfer for antivenom.

misconceptions.label: Enzyme kinetics
misconceptions.misconception: A competitive inhibitor lowers Vmax.
misconceptions.correction: Competitive inhibitors raise Km without changing Vmax; non-competitive inhibitors lower Vmax.

misconceptions.label: Epidemiological study designs
misconceptions.misconception: Case-control studies measure incidence directly.
misconceptions.correction: Case-control studies estimate odds ratios; cohort studies measure incidence and relative risk.

misconceptions.label: Epiglottitis
misconceptions.misconception: The throat of a child with suspected epiglottitis should be examined with a tongue depressor.
misconceptions.correction: Examining the throat can precipitate complete airway obstruction; keep the child calm and secure the airway in a controlled setting.

misconceptions.label: Epistaxis
misconceptions.misconception: Tilt the head back to stop a nosebleed.
misconceptions.correction: Lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose; tilting back makes blood run into the airway and stomach.

misconceptions.label: Facial nerve palsy
misconceptions.misconception: Facial weakness that spares the forehead is Bell palsy.
misconceptions.correction: Forehead sparing suggests an upper motor neuron lesion such as stroke; Bell palsy involves the forehead.

misconceptions.label: Febrile seizures
misconceptions.misconception: Febrile seizures mean the child has epilepsy.
misconceptions.correction: Simple febrile seizures carry only a small added risk of epilepsy and do not need long-term antiseizure medicines.

misconceptions.label: Fever
misconceptions.misconception: Fever should always be suppressed with antipyretics.
misconceptions.correction: Antipyretics are for comfort; the cause matters more, and fever height does not reliably indicate severity.

misconceptions.label: Fibrinolytics
misconceptions.misconception: Thrombolysis is useful at any time after a stroke.
misconceptions.correction: Benefit is strictly time-dependent within a narrow window, and haemorrhage must be excluded first.

misconceptions.label: Foreign body aspiration
misconceptions.misconception: A normal chest X-ray excludes foreign body aspiration.
misconceptions.correction: Most aspirated objects are radiolucent; history is key and bronchoscopy is diagnostic.

misconceptions.label: Fracture complications
misconceptions.misconception: Compartment syndrome can be excluded if distal pulses are present.
misconceptions.correction: Pulses are often preserved; pain out of proportion and pain on passive stretch are early signs.

misconceptions.label: Gastrointestinal bleeding
misconceptions.misconception: Melaena always means bleeding from the upper GI tract.
misconceptions.correction: Melaena usually indicates a source proximal to the ligament of Treitz, but small-bowel or right-colon bleeding with slow transit can also cause it.

misconceptions.label: Glycated haemoglobin
misconceptions.misconception: HbA1c reflects blood glucose over the previous week.
misconceptions.correction: HbA1c reflects average glucose over about 2–3 months, and is unreliable in haemolysis and haemoglobinopathies.

misconceptions.label: Gout
misconceptions.misconception: A normal serum uric acid during an attack excludes gout.
misconceptions.correction: Uric acid can be normal during an acute attack; joint aspiration showing urate crystals is diagnostic.

misconceptions.label: Gram staining
misconceptions.misconception: Gram-positive bacteria stain pink.
misconceptions.correction: Gram-positive organisms retain crystal violet and stain purple; Gram-negative ones stain pink with the counterstain.

misconceptions.label: Haemodynamics
misconceptions.misconception: Halving the radius of a vessel halves the flow through it.
misconceptions.correction: By Poiseuille's law flow varies with the fourth power of radius, so halving the radius cuts flow about sixteen-fold.

misconceptions.label: Haemoglobin
misconceptions.misconception: A right shift of the oxygen dissociation curve means haemoglobin holds oxygen more tightly.
misconceptions.correction: A right shift (raised CO2, H+, temperature, 2,3-BPG) lowers affinity and releases more oxygen to tissues.

misconceptions.label: Haemostasis
misconceptions.misconception: Bleeding time tests the coagulation factors.
misconceptions.correction: Bleeding time reflects platelet function and vessel response; PT and aPTT test coagulation factors.

misconceptions.label: Hand hygiene
misconceptions.misconception: Wearing gloves removes the need for hand hygiene.
misconceptions.correction: Hand hygiene is needed before and after glove use; gloves can be contaminated or have micro-defects.

misconceptions.label: Hanging
misconceptions.misconception: The ligature mark in hanging is horizontal and complete.
misconceptions.correction: In hanging the mark is usually oblique and incomplete; a horizontal complete mark suggests strangulation.

misconceptions.label: Head injury
misconceptions.misconception: A lucid interval means the head injury is not serious.
misconceptions.correction: A lucid interval is typical of extradural haematoma, which can deteriorate rapidly.

misconceptions.label: Headache
misconceptions.misconception: A sudden severe headache that settles with analgesics is unlikely to be serious.
misconceptions.correction: Thunderclap headache needs evaluation for subarachnoid haemorrhage regardless of response to analgesia.

misconceptions.label: Heart failure
misconceptions.misconception: Heart failure always means a low ejection fraction.
misconceptions.correction: About half of patients have preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), with diastolic dysfunction as the main problem.

misconceptions.label: Helicobacter pylori infection
misconceptions.misconception: A urea breath test is reliable while the patient is on proton pump inhibitors.
misconceptions.correction: PPIs and recent antibiotics cause false negatives; stop them before testing.

misconceptions.label: Herd immunity
misconceptions.misconception: Herd immunity protects everyone once a few people are vaccinated.
misconceptions.correction: Herd immunity requires coverage above a threshold that depends on the disease's transmissibility.

misconceptions.label: Hernia
misconceptions.misconception: An inguinal hernia that reduces easily never needs surgery.
misconceptions.correction: Inguinal hernias carry a risk of incarceration and strangulation; repair is usually advised, especially in children.

misconceptions.label: HIV infection
misconceptions.misconception: A negative HIV antibody test soon after exposure excludes infection.
misconceptions.correction: Tests can be negative in the window period; repeat testing is needed after exposure.

misconceptions.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
misconceptions.misconception: Painful lymph nodes are typical of lymphoma.
misconceptions.correction: Lymphoma nodes are typically painless and rubbery; pain is more typical of infection (alcohol-induced pain is a rare exception).

misconceptions.label: Hookworm infection
misconceptions.misconception: Hookworm infection spreads mainly through contaminated food.
misconceptions.correction: Larvae penetrate the skin, usually through bare feet on contaminated soil.

misconceptions.label: Hypercalcaemia
misconceptions.misconception: Most hypercalcaemia in hospital patients is due to primary hyperparathyroidism.
misconceptions.correction: Primary hyperparathyroidism is commonest in outpatients; malignancy is the leading cause in hospitalised patients.

misconceptions.label: Hyperkalaemia
misconceptions.misconception: Calcium gluconate lowers serum potassium in hyperkalaemia.
misconceptions.correction: Calcium only stabilises the cardiac membrane; insulin-glucose and beta-agonists shift potassium into cells, and binders or dialysis remove it.

misconceptions.label: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state
misconceptions.misconception: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state is just a milder form of diabetic ketoacidosis.
misconceptions.correction: It has higher mortality, marked dehydration and hyperosmolality with little ketosis, and needs slower, fluid-led correction.

misconceptions.label: Hypersensitivity reactions
misconceptions.misconception: Anaphylaxis is a type IV hypersensitivity reaction.
misconceptions.correction: Anaphylaxis is a type I IgE-mediated immediate reaction; type IV is delayed and T-cell mediated.

misconceptions.label: Hypertension
misconceptions.misconception: Hypertension causes headache, so a patient without symptoms is unlikely to be hypertensive.
misconceptions.correction: Hypertension is usually asymptomatic until organ damage occurs; it is detected by measurement, not symptoms.

misconceptions.label: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
misconceptions.misconception: Pre-eclampsia always resolves the moment the baby is delivered.
misconceptions.correction: Eclampsia and severe features can occur postpartum, usually within the first days; monitoring continues after delivery.

misconceptions.label: Hypertensive emergencies
misconceptions.misconception: Blood pressure in a hypertensive emergency should be brought to normal as fast as possible.
misconceptions.correction: Lower mean arterial pressure by no more than about 25% in the first hour; rapid normalisation risks cerebral, coronary and renal ischaemia.

misconceptions.label: Hypoglycaemia
misconceptions.misconception: A conscious patient with hypoglycaemia needs intravenous dextrose.
misconceptions.correction: If the patient can swallow, oral fast-acting glucose is first-line; IV dextrose or glucagon is for those who cannot.

misconceptions.label: Hypokalaemia
misconceptions.misconception: Potassium replacement will correct hypokalaemia even if magnesium is low.
misconceptions.correction: Hypomagnesaemia causes ongoing renal potassium loss; magnesium must be corrected for potassium to normalise.

misconceptions.label: Hyponatraemia
misconceptions.misconception: All hyponatraemia should be treated with normal saline.
misconceptions.correction: Treatment depends on volume status: saline for hypovolaemia but fluid restriction for SIADH; correct chronic hyponatraemia slowly to avoid osmotic demyelination.

misconceptions.label: Hypothyroidism
misconceptions.misconception: Thyroxine should be started at full dose in all patients.
misconceptions.correction: Older adults and those with heart disease start low and titrate slowly to avoid precipitating ischaemia.

misconceptions.label: Hypoxia
misconceptions.misconception: Carbon monoxide poisoning lowers the measured arterial PaO2.
misconceptions.correction: PaO2 is often normal; CO blocks oxygen carriage by haemoglobin, so pulse oximetry and PaO2 can mislead.

misconceptions.label: Imaging safety
misconceptions.misconception: MRI uses ionising radiation.
misconceptions.correction: MRI uses magnetic fields and radio waves; CT and X-ray use ionising radiation.

misconceptions.label: Immune thrombocytopenia
misconceptions.misconception: Every child with immune thrombocytopenia needs platelet transfusion.
misconceptions.correction: Most childhood ITP resolves spontaneously; transfusion is for life-threatening bleeding only, because platelets are rapidly destroyed.

misconceptions.label: Inborn errors of amino acid metabolism
misconceptions.misconception: Phenylketonuria is treated by removing phenylalanine completely from the diet.
misconceptions.correction: Phenylalanine is essential; it is restricted, not eliminated, and tyrosine becomes essential.

misconceptions.label: Infective endocarditis
misconceptions.misconception: A negative single blood culture excludes infective endocarditis.
misconceptions.correction: At least three sets from separate sites are needed before antibiotics; culture-negative endocarditis also exists.

misconceptions.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
misconceptions.misconception: Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis both affect only the colon.
misconceptions.correction: Crohn disease can affect any part of the GI tract with skip lesions; ulcerative colitis is continuous from the rectum.

misconceptions.label: Informed consent
misconceptions.misconception: A signed consent form alone proves valid informed consent.
misconceptions.correction: Valid consent needs capacity, adequate information, voluntariness and understanding; the form only documents it.

misconceptions.label: Intrauterine contraceptive device
misconceptions.misconception: An IUCD works mainly by causing abortion.
misconceptions.correction: Copper IUCDs act mainly by preventing fertilisation through spermicidal effects.

misconceptions.label: Iron deficiency anaemia
misconceptions.misconception: A normal serum ferritin excludes iron deficiency in an inflamed patient.
misconceptions.correction: Ferritin is an acute-phase reactant; it may be normal or high despite iron deficiency in inflammation.

misconceptions.label: Jaundice
misconceptions.misconception: Jaundice with dark urine means haemolysis.
misconceptions.correction: Dark urine reflects conjugated bilirubin (hepatic or obstructive); haemolytic jaundice is acholuric.

misconceptions.label: Kawasaki disease
misconceptions.misconception: Kawasaki disease is a self-limiting rash illness without serious consequences.
misconceptions.correction: Untreated, it can cause coronary artery aneurysms; IVIG within 10 days reduces this risk.

misconceptions.label: Leprosy
misconceptions.misconception: Leprosy is highly contagious through brief skin contact.
misconceptions.correction: Transmission needs prolonged close contact, mainly via nasal droplets; most people are naturally resistant and treated patients are non-infectious.

misconceptions.label: Leukaemias
misconceptions.misconception: A normal white cell count excludes leukaemia.
misconceptions.correction: Leukaemia can present with a low or normal count; the blood film and bone marrow are diagnostic.

misconceptions.label: Levels of prevention
misconceptions.misconception: Screening is primary prevention.
misconceptions.correction: Screening is secondary prevention (early detection); primary prevention stops disease occurring.

misconceptions.label: Lipoproteins
misconceptions.misconception: HDL carries cholesterol from the liver to tissues.
misconceptions.correction: HDL mediates reverse cholesterol transport from tissues to the liver; LDL delivers cholesterol to tissues.

misconceptions.label: Liver disease
misconceptions.misconception: Normal transaminases exclude significant liver disease.
misconceptions.correction: Transaminases may be normal in compensated cirrhosis; synthetic function (albumin, INR) and imaging matter more.

misconceptions.label: Lung carcinoma
misconceptions.misconception: Lung cancer occurs only in smokers.
misconceptions.correction: Smoking is the main risk, but adenocarcinoma occurs in never-smokers, and occupational exposures also contribute.

misconceptions.label: Lymphatic filariasis
misconceptions.misconception: Filariasis is spread by Anopheles mosquitoes only in India.
misconceptions.correction: In India, Culex quinquefasciatus is the main vector of Wuchereria bancrofti.

misconceptions.label: Malaria
misconceptions.misconception: A single negative smear rules out malaria.
misconceptions.correction: Repeat smears or rapid tests at intervals are needed when clinical suspicion persists.

misconceptions.label: Measures of morbidity and mortality
misconceptions.misconception: Prevalence and incidence mean the same thing.
misconceptions.correction: Incidence counts new cases over time; prevalence counts all existing cases at a point or period.

misconceptions.label: Medical negligence
misconceptions.misconception: Any bad outcome after treatment is medical negligence.
misconceptions.correction: Negligence requires a duty of care, a breach of the standard of care, and harm caused by that breach.

misconceptions.label: Megaloblastic anaemia
misconceptions.misconception: Folic acid alone is safe treatment for any macrocytic anaemia.
misconceptions.correction: Folate alone in B12 deficiency can worsen neurological damage; check and replace B12 first.

misconceptions.label: Membrane potentials
misconceptions.misconception: The resting membrane potential is mainly due to sodium.
misconceptions.correction: It is mainly due to potassium leak through open K+ channels, maintained by the Na+/K+ pump.

misconceptions.label: Meningitis
misconceptions.misconception: Lumbar puncture must always be done before antibiotics in suspected meningitis.
misconceptions.correction: Antibiotics should not be delayed; if LP is delayed (e.g. for CT), take blood cultures and give antibiotics first.

misconceptions.label: Menstrual cycle
misconceptions.misconception: Ovulation occurs on day 14 in every woman.
misconceptions.correction: The luteal phase is relatively fixed (about 14 days); ovulation timing varies with cycle length.

misconceptions.label: Metastasis
misconceptions.misconception: Carcinomas mainly spread through the blood and sarcomas through lymphatics.
misconceptions.correction: Carcinomas typically spread first by lymphatics and sarcomas by blood (with exceptions such as RCC, HCC, follicular thyroid).

misconceptions.label: Multiple myeloma
misconceptions.misconception: Myeloma lesions are reliably detected by a bone scan.
misconceptions.correction: Lytic myeloma lesions often do not show on isotope bone scan; a skeletal survey, CT or MRI is used.

misconceptions.label: Myasthenia gravis
misconceptions.misconception: Weakness in myasthenia gravis is worst in the morning.
misconceptions.correction: Weakness worsens with activity and later in the day (fatigability).

misconceptions.label: Necrosis
misconceptions.misconception: Apoptosis and necrosis both cause inflammation.
misconceptions.correction: Necrosis provokes inflammation; apoptosis is programmed cell death with intact membranes and little inflammation.

misconceptions.label: Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia
misconceptions.misconception: Jaundice in the first 24 hours of life is physiological.
misconceptions.correction: Jaundice within 24 hours is always pathological, often haemolytic, and needs urgent evaluation.

misconceptions.label: Neonatal sepsis
misconceptions.misconception: A newborn with sepsis will usually have a high fever.
misconceptions.correction: Neonatal sepsis often presents with hypothermia, poor feeding, lethargy or apnoea rather than fever.

misconceptions.label: Nephrotic syndrome
misconceptions.misconception: Nephrotic syndrome causes visible blood in the urine.
misconceptions.correction: Nephrotic syndrome features heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia and oedema; haematuria and hypertension point to nephritic syndrome.

misconceptions.label: Neuromuscular transmission
misconceptions.misconception: Curare blocks acetylcholine release.
misconceptions.correction: Curare competitively blocks nicotinic receptors at the end-plate; botulinum toxin blocks acetylcholine release.

misconceptions.label: Non-opioid analgesics
misconceptions.misconception: Paracetamol is safe in any dose because it is available over the counter.
misconceptions.correction: Overdose causes hepatotoxicity; N-acetylcysteine is the antidote.

misconceptions.label: Ocular trauma
misconceptions.misconception: Chemical eye injury should first be examined to identify the chemical.
misconceptions.correction: Immediate copious irrigation comes first; identification and examination follow.

misconceptions.label: Oedema
misconceptions.misconception: All oedema should be treated with diuretics.
misconceptions.correction: Treat the cause; diuretics may harm in hypovolaemia, and lymphoedema or venous oedema responds poorly.

misconceptions.label: Open fractures
misconceptions.misconception: Antibiotics in open fractures can wait until surgery.
misconceptions.correction: Give antibiotics and tetanus cover as early as possible; delay increases infection.

misconceptions.label: Opioid analgesics
misconceptions.misconception: Patients with cancer pain on opioids quickly become addicted.
misconceptions.correction: Addiction is uncommon when opioids are used appropriately for cancer pain; tolerance and dependence are different from addiction.

misconceptions.label: Opportunistic infections
misconceptions.misconception: Opportunistic infections occur only in HIV infection.
misconceptions.correction: They occur in any significant immunosuppression, including chemotherapy, transplantation and long-term steroids.

misconceptions.label: Oral rehydration therapy
misconceptions.misconception: ORS stops diarrhoea.
misconceptions.correction: ORS replaces losses and prevents dehydration; it does not reduce stool output (zinc shortens the illness).

misconceptions.label: Osteoarthritis
misconceptions.misconception: Osteoarthritis is an inflammatory arthritis with prolonged morning stiffness.
misconceptions.correction: Osteoarthritis is degenerative, with brief (<30 min) stiffness; prolonged stiffness suggests inflammatory arthritis.

misconceptions.label: Osteoporosis
misconceptions.misconception: Osteoporosis causes bone pain before fractures occur.
misconceptions.correction: Osteoporosis is silent until a fracture; diagnosis is by bone density.

misconceptions.label: Oxygen therapy
misconceptions.misconception: More oxygen is always better for a breathless patient.
misconceptions.correction: Titrate to target saturations; hyperoxia harms some patients, including those with hypercapnia and preterm infants.

misconceptions.label: Palliative care
misconceptions.misconception: Palliative care is only for the last days of life.
misconceptions.correction: Palliative care can begin at diagnosis of serious illness alongside curative treatment.

misconceptions.label: Pancreatitis
misconceptions.misconception: The height of serum amylase or lipase indicates the severity of pancreatitis.
misconceptions.correction: Enzyme levels support diagnosis but do not predict severity; clinical scores and organ failure do.

misconceptions.label: Paraneoplastic syndromes
misconceptions.misconception: Paraneoplastic syndromes are caused by direct spread of the tumour.
misconceptions.correction: They are caused by hormones, cytokines or antibodies produced by or against the tumour, at sites remote from it.

misconceptions.label: Peptic ulcer disease
misconceptions.misconception: Stress and spicy food are the main causes of peptic ulcers.
misconceptions.correction: Helicobacter pylori and NSAIDs are the main causes.

misconceptions.label: Peripheral arterial disease
misconceptions.misconception: Leg pain on walking is usually due to arthritis.
misconceptions.correction: Calf pain on walking relieved by rest suggests intermittent claudication; check pulses and ankle-brachial index.

misconceptions.label: Peripheral nerve injury
misconceptions.misconception: Loss of sensation and loss of power always occur together after nerve injury.
misconceptions.correction: Pure motor, pure sensory or mixed deficits depend on the nerve and level injured.

misconceptions.label: Pesticide poisoning
misconceptions.misconception: Atropine should be stopped as soon as pupils dilate in organophosphate poisoning.
misconceptions.correction: Atropinisation is titrated to drying of secretions and adequate heart rate and BP, not pupil size.

misconceptions.label: Pharmacokinetics
misconceptions.misconception: Doubling the dose doubles the duration of drug action.
misconceptions.correction: With first-order kinetics, doubling the dose prolongs action by about one half-life only.

misconceptions.label: Pleural fluid analysis
misconceptions.misconception: An exudate is diagnosed only by high pleural protein.
misconceptions.correction: Light's criteria use protein and LDH ratios and pleural LDH; any one criterion classifies the fluid as an exudate.

misconceptions.label: Pneumonia
misconceptions.misconception: A normal chest examination rules out pneumonia.
misconceptions.correction: Examination is insensitive; a chest X-ray is needed when pneumonia is suspected.

misconceptions.label: Polycystic ovary syndrome
misconceptions.misconception: Polycystic ovaries on ultrasound alone diagnose PCOS.
misconceptions.correction: Diagnosis needs two of three (Rotterdam): oligo-anovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries, after excluding other causes.

misconceptions.label: Polymerase chain reaction
misconceptions.misconception: A positive PCR always means live, active infection.
misconceptions.correction: PCR detects nucleic acid, which can persist after the organism is dead or the infection is cleared.

misconceptions.label: Porphyrias
misconceptions.misconception: All porphyrias cause skin photosensitivity.
misconceptions.correction: Acute intermittent porphyria causes neurovisceral attacks without photosensitivity.

misconceptions.label: Postmenopausal bleeding
misconceptions.misconception: A small amount of postmenopausal bleeding is normal.
misconceptions.correction: Any postmenopausal bleeding needs evaluation to exclude endometrial cancer.

misconceptions.label: Postpartum haemorrhage
misconceptions.misconception: Most postpartum haemorrhage is due to retained placenta.
misconceptions.correction: Uterine atony is the commonest cause (the 4 Ts: tone, trauma, tissue, thrombin).

misconceptions.label: Preoperative assessment
misconceptions.misconception: All patients must stop all medicines before surgery.
misconceptions.correction: Many drugs (e.g. beta-blockers, most antihypertensives) continue; some (anticoagulants, certain antidiabetics) are adjusted.

misconceptions.label: Prescribing in special populations
misconceptions.misconception: Most drugs are safe in pregnancy if they are safe in adults.
misconceptions.correction: Teratogenicity and altered pharmacokinetics mean drugs need specific pregnancy safety data.

misconceptions.label: Preterm labour
misconceptions.misconception: Tocolytics should be continued until term to prevent preterm birth.
misconceptions.correction: Tocolysis is short-term, mainly to allow antenatal corticosteroids and transfer; it does not prolong pregnancy to term.

misconceptions.label: Primary open-angle glaucoma
misconceptions.misconception: Glaucoma always causes eye pain.
misconceptions.correction: Open-angle glaucoma is painless and silent until advanced visual field loss.

misconceptions.label: Prostate cancer
misconceptions.misconception: A normal PSA excludes prostate cancer.
misconceptions.correction: PSA has limited sensitivity and specificity; examination and further tests are needed when suspicion exists.

misconceptions.label: Protein-energy malnutrition
misconceptions.misconception: Kwashiorkor and marasmus are both defined by severe wasting.
misconceptions.correction: Oedema is the hallmark of kwashiorkor; marasmus is severe wasting without oedema.

misconceptions.label: Psoriasis
misconceptions.misconception: Psoriasis is contagious.
misconceptions.correction: Psoriasis is an immune-mediated disease and is not infectious.

misconceptions.label: Pulmonary function tests
misconceptions.misconception: A reduced FEV1 always means obstructive lung disease.
misconceptions.correction: FEV1 falls in both patterns; the FEV1/FVC ratio is low in obstruction and normal or high in restriction.

misconceptions.label: Pulmonary tuberculosis
misconceptions.misconception: A negative sputum smear excludes pulmonary tuberculosis.
misconceptions.correction: Smear has limited sensitivity; nucleic acid amplification tests (e.g. CBNAAT) and culture are more sensitive.

misconceptions.label: Pyrexia of unknown origin
misconceptions.misconception: Any fever without an obvious source is a PUO.
misconceptions.correction: PUO requires prolonged fever (classically >3 weeks) undiagnosed despite a defined period of investigation.

misconceptions.label: Rabies
misconceptions.misconception: Rabies post-exposure prophylaxis can be skipped if the animal looks healthy.
misconceptions.correction: Category II–III exposures need prophylaxis started immediately; observation of a dog or cat can only stop it later.

misconceptions.label: Radiation protection
misconceptions.misconception: Lead aprons make radiation exposure harmless at any distance or time.
misconceptions.correction: Protection relies on time, distance and shielding together.

misconceptions.label: Red eye
misconceptions.misconception: Topical steroids are a safe first treatment for any red eye.
misconceptions.correction: Steroids can worsen herpetic and fungal keratitis and cause glaucoma; diagnose first.

misconceptions.label: Regional anaesthesia
misconceptions.misconception: Spinal and epidural anaesthesia are the same.
misconceptions.correction: Spinal is injected into the subarachnoid space with rapid dense block; epidural is outside the dura, slower, and can be titrated by catheter.

misconceptions.label: Regulation of respiration
misconceptions.misconception: Low oxygen is the main normal drive to breathe.
misconceptions.correction: Arterial CO2 (via central chemoreceptors) is the main normal drive; hypoxic drive matters mainly in hypoxaemia.

misconceptions.label: Renal regulation of fluid, electrolytes and acid-base
misconceptions.misconception: Aldosterone acts mainly to retain water.
misconceptions.correction: Aldosterone increases sodium reabsorption and potassium and H+ secretion; ADH mainly regulates water.

misconceptions.label: Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors
misconceptions.misconception: ACE inhibitors and ARBs should be combined for extra kidney protection.
misconceptions.correction: Dual blockade increases hyperkalaemia and kidney injury without added benefit.

misconceptions.label: Rh isoimmunisation
misconceptions.misconception: Anti-D is needed for Rh-positive mothers.
misconceptions.correction: Anti-D prophylaxis is for unsensitised Rh-negative mothers carrying a possibly Rh-positive fetus.

misconceptions.label: Rheumatic heart disease
misconceptions.misconception: The aortic valve is the valve most commonly affected in rheumatic heart disease.
misconceptions.correction: The mitral valve is most commonly involved, followed by the aortic valve.

misconceptions.label: Rheumatoid arthritis
misconceptions.misconception: A negative rheumatoid factor excludes rheumatoid arthritis.
misconceptions.correction: Up to a third of patients are seronegative; anti-CCP is more specific and diagnosis is clinical.

misconceptions.label: Scabies
misconceptions.misconception: Only the person with the itch needs scabies treatment.
misconceptions.correction: All close contacts are treated at the same time, and clothes and bedding are washed, to prevent reinfestation.

misconceptions.label: Schizophrenia
misconceptions.misconception: Schizophrenia means having a split personality.
misconceptions.correction: Schizophrenia is a psychotic disorder; split or multiple personality refers to dissociative identity disorder.

misconceptions.label: Screening for disease
misconceptions.misconception: A test with high sensitivity is best for confirming a diagnosis.
misconceptions.correction: High sensitivity helps rule out disease (SnNout); high specificity helps rule it in (SpPin).

misconceptions.label: Sepsis
misconceptions.misconception: Sepsis requires a fever.
misconceptions.correction: Older, immunosuppressed and very ill patients may be normothermic or hypothermic; hypothermia is a poor prognostic sign.

misconceptions.label: Serological tests
misconceptions.misconception: A positive IgG antibody indicates current infection.
misconceptions.correction: IgM suggests recent infection; IgG usually indicates past infection or immunity unless titres rise.

misconceptions.label: Severe acute malnutrition
misconceptions.misconception: Children with severe acute malnutrition should be given high-calorie feeds at once.
misconceptions.correction: Start cautiously with F-75 in the stabilisation phase to avoid refeeding problems, then progress to F-100 or RUTF.

misconceptions.label: Shock
misconceptions.misconception: Normal blood pressure excludes shock.
misconceptions.correction: Compensated shock maintains BP; tachycardia, raised lactate, poor perfusion and low urine output appear first.

misconceptions.label: Sickle cell disease
misconceptions.misconception: Sickle cell trait carriers commonly have painful crises.
misconceptions.correction: Trait is usually asymptomatic; crises occur in homozygous sickle cell disease.

misconceptions.label: Spinal injuries
misconceptions.misconception: An alert patient who moves all limbs cannot have an unstable spinal injury.
misconceptions.correction: Unstable injuries can exist without deficits; immobilise until cleared clinically or by imaging.

misconceptions.label: Sterilisation
misconceptions.misconception: Disinfection and sterilisation mean the same thing.
misconceptions.correction: Sterilisation kills all microbes including spores; disinfection reduces pathogens but may not kill spores.

misconceptions.label: Stridor
misconceptions.misconception: Stridor and wheeze come from the same part of the airway.
misconceptions.correction: Stridor arises from the larynx or upper airway; wheeze from narrowed lower airways.

misconceptions.label: Stroke
misconceptions.misconception: A normal early CT scan rules out ischaemic stroke.
misconceptions.correction: Early CT is often normal in ischaemic stroke; its main early role is to exclude haemorrhage before thrombolysis.

misconceptions.label: Syncope
misconceptions.misconception: Syncope with jerking movements is always a seizure.
misconceptions.correction: Brief myoclonic jerks are common in syncope; rapid recovery without prolonged confusion favours syncope.

misconceptions.label: Syphilis
misconceptions.misconception: Syphilis is cured once the primary ulcer heals.
misconceptions.correction: The chancre heals without treatment while infection progresses to secondary and later stages.

misconceptions.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
misconceptions.misconception: A positive ANA test confirms lupus.
misconceptions.correction: ANA is sensitive but not specific; healthy people can be positive. Anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm are more specific.

misconceptions.label: Tests of significance
misconceptions.misconception: A p-value below 0.05 means the result is clinically important.
misconceptions.correction: Statistical significance does not measure effect size or clinical importance; confidence intervals help.

misconceptions.label: Thalassaemia
misconceptions.misconception: Thalassaemia trait needs iron supplements because the cells are microcytic.
misconceptions.correction: Iron stores are normal in trait; unnecessary iron risks overload. Distinguish it from iron deficiency with iron studies and HbA2.

misconceptions.label: Thrombosis
misconceptions.misconception: A normal D-dimer excludes DVT in any patient.
misconceptions.correction: D-dimer only helps exclude DVT when pre-test probability is low; high-probability patients need imaging.

misconceptions.label: Thyroid disorders
misconceptions.misconception: A normal TSH excludes all thyroid disease.
misconceptions.correction: TSH can be misleading in pituitary disease, recent treatment change and non-thyroidal illness; free T4 is needed in those settings.

misconceptions.label: Thyroid gland
misconceptions.misconception: T4 is the main active thyroid hormone in tissues.
misconceptions.correction: T4 is mainly a prohormone; it is converted to the more active T3 in peripheral tissues.

misconceptions.label: Thyrotoxicosis
misconceptions.misconception: All thyrotoxicosis is Graves disease and needs antithyroid drugs.
misconceptions.correction: Thyroiditis causes transient thyrotoxicosis from release of stored hormone; antithyroid drugs do not help it.

misconceptions.label: Time since death
misconceptions.misconception: Rigor mortis appears first in the legs.
misconceptions.correction: Rigor typically appears first in the small muscles, such as the eyelids and jaw, and proceeds downward.

misconceptions.label: Transport of respiratory gases
misconceptions.misconception: Most carbon dioxide is carried in blood bound to haemoglobin.
misconceptions.correction: Most CO2 (about 70%) is carried as bicarbonate; smaller amounts are carbamino compounds and dissolved gas.

misconceptions.label: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
misconceptions.misconception: Type 1 diabetes occurs only in children.
misconceptions.correction: Type 1 diabetes can begin at any age, including adulthood.

misconceptions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
misconceptions.misconception: Type 2 diabetes never needs insulin.
misconceptions.correction: Many patients need insulin as beta-cell function declines, or during illness, surgery or pregnancy.

misconceptions.label: Undescended testis
misconceptions.misconception: Undescended testis can wait until puberty for treatment.
misconceptions.correction: Orchidopexy is advised early (around 6–18 months) to protect fertility and allow cancer surveillance.

misconceptions.label: Upper and lower motor neuron lesions
misconceptions.misconception: Acute upper motor neuron lesions always cause spasticity and brisk reflexes.
misconceptions.correction: In the acute phase (spinal or cerebral shock) tone and reflexes may be reduced before UMN signs appear.

misconceptions.label: Urinary tract infection
misconceptions.misconception: Bacteria in the urine always need antibiotics.
misconceptions.correction: Asymptomatic bacteriuria is usually not treated, except in pregnancy and before urological procedures.

misconceptions.label: Urine formation
misconceptions.misconception: Most filtered water is reabsorbed in the collecting duct.
misconceptions.correction: About two-thirds is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule; the collecting duct fine-tunes reabsorption under ADH.

misconceptions.label: Urolithiasis
misconceptions.misconception: All kidney stones are visible on plain X-ray.
misconceptions.correction: Uric acid stones are radiolucent; non-contrast CT is the most sensitive test.

misconceptions.label: Urticaria
misconceptions.misconception: Hives always mean an allergy to food.
misconceptions.correction: Most chronic urticaria is idiopathic or autoimmune; acute cases also follow infections and drugs.

misconceptions.label: Vaccine-preventable diseases
misconceptions.misconception: A mild fever or cold is a reason to delay vaccination.
misconceptions.correction: Minor illness is not a contraindication; only moderate or severe acute illness justifies deferral.

misconceptions.label: Vaccines
misconceptions.misconception: Live vaccines are safe in all immunocompromised patients.
misconceptions.correction: Live vaccines are generally contraindicated in significant immunosuppression and pregnancy.

misconceptions.label: Valvular heart disease
misconceptions.misconception: The loudness of a murmur reflects the severity of the valve lesion.
misconceptions.correction: Loudness correlates poorly with severity; in severe aortic stenosis the murmur may soften as cardiac output falls.

misconceptions.label: Varicocele
misconceptions.misconception: A varicocele that does not empty on lying down is harmless.
misconceptions.correction: A non-reducing or new right-sided varicocele can indicate retroperitoneal or renal pathology.

misconceptions.label: Viral hepatitis
misconceptions.misconception: Hepatitis A commonly becomes chronic.
misconceptions.correction: Hepatitis A and E do not usually cause chronic infection; hepatitis B and C do.

misconceptions.label: Vitamins
misconceptions.misconception: Large doses of fat-soluble vitamins are harmless because excess is excreted.
misconceptions.correction: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) accumulate and can cause toxicity.

misconceptions.label: Vitiligo
misconceptions.misconception: Vitiligo is a form of leprosy.
misconceptions.correction: Vitiligo is autoimmune depigmentation with normal sensation; leprosy patches are hypopigmented with sensory loss.

misconceptions.label: Wound care
misconceptions.misconception: Antiseptics should be applied repeatedly to all clean wounds.
misconceptions.correction: Repeated strong antiseptics can damage healing tissue; clean with saline and keep the wound moist and covered.

misconceptions.label: Ziehl-Neelsen staining
misconceptions.misconception: Ziehl-Neelsen stain is used for all bacteria.
misconceptions.correction: It detects acid-fast organisms such as mycobacteria, which resist decolourisation with acid-alcohol.
